Troubleshooting and FAQ

Start with /sigma-doctor. If it does not name the problem, find the symptom below.

On this page
  • Read the doctor first
  • Symptom, cause, fix
  • Why was my goal not picked
  • Reading a resource hold
  • Install differences on Cursor and Antigravity
  • FAQ

Most people only need

  • Run /sigma-doctor. Every MISSING row carries its own fix command.
  • A refused verify is almost always the per-checkout trust, granted once with a git config line.
  • A merge held on a private repository usually means GitHub refused to show the branch protection.
  • Nothing merges by itself on the defaults, so a pull request left open is normal.

Most failures in Sigma stop and say why rather than guess: a refused command, a hold with a reason, a goal parked with a question. This page maps what you see to what caused it and what to run. Every command here was read from the documentation and the code; where something was not run, it says so.

Read the doctor first

/sigma-doctor checks only what your .sdlc/config.json makes relevant, so a local-files project sees few rows and a GitHub project with a board and a ledger sees many. OK means ready. MISSING means run the printed one-liner. A row ending (cannot verify) is not a pass. It never runs an interactive login or a package install for you.

On a narrow screen, scroll the table sideways.

RowWhat it meansFix
project layerNo .sdlc here, or it is incomplete./sigma-init
config.json is valid JSONA stray comma or quote.Fix the syntax; keep the file valid after each edit.
git repository, git remote, base branchNot a repository, no usable origin, or the base branch was never pushed.Add the remote and push, or go local-only (--local-only). Nothing flips this silently.
gh installed, gh auth, gh token scopes, gh project scopegh is absent, logged out, or short of a scope.The printed gh auth refresh -s <scope> line. Run it yourself.
verify command trusted in this checkoutThe checkout has not granted the verify command.The trust line below.
verify.command resolves in the goal worktreeThe command uses a path that exists only in your checkout.Use an absolute interpreter path, an activated environment on PATH, or a wrapper script.
secret-shaped files are ignoredA file named like a secret (.env, a key, a credentials file) is not ignored and could be staged. It matches names only and never reads a file.Add the paths to .gitignore. Only a real fixture belongs in work.allow_secret_paths.
team ledger initializedThe ledger is on in config but its branch is not set up in this clone./sigma-ledger. It is safe to re-run and each teammate runs it once.
no leftover watcher stop fileA stop file exists with no watcher running, so a new watcher exits at once.rm .sdlc/state/watch.stop
running watcher matches installed buildThe watcher started before you updated.touch .sdlc/state/watch.stop; the next trigger restarts it.
goals awaiting mergeA pull request is open and waiting for you, with its age.Merge or close it.
resource admission, resource stale leasesThe memory guard is holding work, or dead processes still hold leases.See Reading a resource hold.
sigma install scopes, sigma up to dateOne scope is below the version floor, or you are behind the marketplace.Updating the plugin
coexistenceThe previous plugin is also active. A warning, never a failure.Switching over

Symptom, cause, fix

SymptomCauseFix
Verify exits with REFUSED: repository-configured shell command requires explicit operator trust; no goal reaches doneThe verify command comes from a file in the repository. Trust is stored in this checkout's own git config and is not cloned, so every new clone must grant it. Until it does, the command is refused.Inspect verify.command, then run once: git -C <project> config --local sigma.allowRepositoryShellCommands true. Re-running /sigma-init prints a [trust] verify line with this gesture.
The loop opens a pull request but will not merge it, saying protection could not be determinedOn a private repository on a GitHub free plan, the branch-protection and rules reads are refused with HTTP 403. Sigma then holds the merge rather than claim that nothing is enforced. Measured once, by hand, on a free-plan private repository on 18 Nov 2026.Merge by hand. Or, if you know the repository has no protection and use work.auto_merge: always, set work.protection_unreadable to "allow" (that exact string). It relaxes only the 403 case; any other read failure still holds, and GitHub still enforces any protection at merge time.
/sigma-goal <N> --land refuses up frontIt needs work.enabled: true and work.auto_merge of protected or always. The default off never merges, so a run that exists to land one goal refuses.Set work.auto_merge once your base branch has protection that requires checks or a second person's approval. Otherwise use /sigma-loop, which leaves the pull request for you.
git status shows .sdlc and .gitignore as untracked after initExpected. Init scaffolds files you have not committed yet.Commit .gitignore, .sdlc/goals/, .sdlc/project.md and .sdlc/config.json. The runtime folders are already ignored. Never ignore .sdlc as a whole (The .sdlc folder).
git pull in the root checkout refuses over untracked .sdlc plan, research or acceptance filesRecords written in the root checkout and not yet committed. A known open problem, not fully solved.Commit them on a branch or move them aside, then pull.
A goal sits at sdlc:in-progress and nothing is working itThat label marks that a session is on it. A session that crashed or slept can leave it. With the ledger on, a claim expires after ledger.lease.ttl_hours (default 12). A goal a dead session claimed but never started is released on the next pick after session_release.grace_minutes (15). A live session holding an unstarted claim longer than session_release.hold_minutes (30; 0 turns it off) has it released too. A started goal is never released automatically.Look first: /sigma-log and /sigma-status. If you know the process is dead, remove sdlc:in-progress and leave sdlc:goal: that puts it back in the queue (Labels).
A goal is parkedIt needs a decision only you can make, or it hit an irreversible or expensive action. Parked goals are collected, not forced.GitHub: /sigma-unpark, which asks why before it re-queues. Local files: edit the goal file, status: parked to status: pending, and delete its entry from .sdlc/state/review-queue.md by hand.
The loop stopped by itselfA budget was reached (max_iterations, max_minutes, max_tokens), the backlog is empty, or the session handed off after 20 goals.Re-run /sigma-loop; a stopped run resumes where it left off. Budgets are on Configuration.
Goals finish but there is no branch or pull requestwork.enabled is off, or you chose local-only. The changes land only in your working tree, while the issue still closes and the record still says done, so nothing looks wrong.Set work.enabled to true (/sigma-init does) if you want a pull request per goal.
The first verify in a goal fails with exit=127A goal's worktree has no installed dependencies, so a relative .venv/bin/python3 or node_modules/.bin/... does not resolve.Absolute interpreter path, an activated environment, or a wrapper script. Anything the command leaves behind (.coverage, build output) must be git-ignored or it rides into the pull request.
A commit is refused naming a fileA secret-shaped file is not ignored. The refusal is the safe outcome.Ignore it. See the doctor row above.
Marking a goal done is refusedNo fresh verify result, or its pull request is not merged yet.Run the verify step; merge the pull request. The loop records done itself after the merge.
/sigma-init exits 2: not a git repository, or github mode needs a repositoryThe directory is not a repository, or origin is not a GitHub repository.git init; or pass --repo OWNER/NAME, or choose --mode local-goals.
A repository hook denies Sigma's editsSigma's implement edits go through the same tool calls a person's would, so your own pre-edit hook applies. It may expect a plan file where Sigma does not write one.Satisfy what the hook expects, or allow Sigma's path. Sigma gets no signal that a host hook was the cause.
In Claude Code's cloud, the setup wizard is silent or the verify command is refusedCloud sessions start from a fresh clone, so trust must be granted again, and they have their own limits.Read Cloud sessions first.

Why was my goal not picked

The loop takes a goal only when every condition below holds. Check them in order.

CheckIf it fails
Open and labelled sdlc:goal (GitHub) or status: pending (local file)The example file ships as proposed and is never picked.
Assigned to youThe shipped config has no filter, but /sigma-init in GitHub mode sets discovery.github.assignee to @me where unset; then only issues assigned to you are worked.
Not sdlc:parked, sdlc:blocked, in progress, or awaiting mergeEach of those holds it out of the queue.
No open prerequisiteA body line **Blocked by:** #N holds it until #N is done (Dependencies and chains).
No live claim by someone elseWith the ledger on, another actor, or another live process of yours, already holds it.
Not outrankedOrder is by priority:P0 to P4, oldest first within a tier; a goal with no priority sorts last.
Ready enoughWith goal_readiness.mode: require, a goal missing its ## Done when section is parked.

Reading a resource hold

When the machine is short of memory, Sigma holds work instead of failing it: goals stay unclaimed and a verify exits without running. A hold is not an error and lifts by itself once the machine is healthy again. /sigma-doctor shows it as a resource admission row.

You seeIt meansDo
open, headroom N MiB, reserve M MiBNothing is held.Nothing.
HELD Nm (reason) with held with N Sigma leasesSigma's own running work is using the memory.Wait. Releasing a lease frees its memory.
HELD with 0 leases: memory is used by other softwareSomething else on the machine holds the memory and Sigma cannot release it.Close other applications; the hold lifts on its own.
The row fails after a hold lasts past the alert timeThe hold has been in place longer than hold_alert_minutes.As above; the row names the tip.
resource stale leases: NLeases belong to dead or expired processes and still count against headroom.Run the sample command the row prints.
resource platform: unsupportedThe guard cannot read this machine, so it refuses rather than guess.Set resource.mode to "off" and cap parallel goals by hand.

resource.mode: observe logs the hold it would make and admits; SIGMA_RESOURCE_MODE overrides the key. The ratios are policy defaults, not calibrated to a real exhaustion. Details: Running unattended and Configuration.

Install differences on Cursor and Antigravity

HostDiffers howMeasured
CursorNo plugin install: clone Sigma to a folder outside the project, then run /sigma-init --cursor in your own repository. Init writes two always-applied rule files that carry the discipline, because Cursor has no hook that Sigma relies on. If the slash command is missing, run the init flow directly from the clone (Get started).Set-up with a board, and one goal to a merged pull request (merged by hand). Not the loop on several goals, hooks, or the command-line agent.
Antigravityagy plugin install converts the Claude Code plugin and skips two hooks (the prompt hook and the skill hook) because Antigravity has no such events. Converted skills still contain a Claude-only folder placeholder, and each carries a note telling the model to use its own folder. /sigma-init --antigravity writes the managed block into AGENTS.md; its wording is Codex's, unadapted.Install and set-up with a board. Not a goal run, the loop, or whether the converted hooks fire.

FAQ

Do I need GitHub?

No. A local-files backlog needs only git, bash and python3. You give up issues, the board, a pull request per goal, its review and the shared ledger sync. See On your own.

Does it work offline?

Sigma is plain scripts that run on your machine and has no server of its own. The agent host it runs inside talks to its model provider, so the host needs its connection. A run with no network at all was not measured.

What does it cost?

The documentation describes no separate Sigma charge; the spend Sigma measures is the model usage your host account bills. Each phase prints its measured cost as it ends, and budgets stop a run. The post-pull-request review is an extra pass per goal, and its cost was measured only once. See Cost and time.

Does it send data anywhere?

Sigma does not report usage data. Your host talks to its model provider under that host's own policy. In GitHub mode, gh and git traffic to GitHub is the default; Slack, a webhook, email and model calls Sigma starts are separate and opt-in. The destination table in the privacy note comes from tracing the code plus one scripted onboarding capture, not a full capture: gh and git launches are recorded but their own connections are outside the capture hook, and the other rows are traced from code, not captured. See also Trust and limits.

Can I use it on a private repository?

Yes. On a free GitHub plan the protection reads fail with a 403 and merges are held; see the second row of the table above.

Will it merge by itself?

Not on the defaults. work.auto_merge ships off: it opens the pull request and you merge it.

Does it touch my main checkout or my branch?

With work.enabled on, each goal runs in its own git worktree on its own branch cut from your base branch, so your checkout does not move. With it off, or local-only, the loop edits your checkout directly.

How do I stop it?

End the session, or stop a run at its budget. For a background watcher, touch .sdlc/state/watch.stop; the unattended supervisor and the Slack listener have supervisor.stop and slack-commands.stop. They check once per tick, so they can take that long to exit. To stop it writing git at all, set work.enabled to false.

How do I see what it did?

/sigma-status for counts and the review queue, /sigma-log for the live trace, the pull request and the issue timeline for the written record, and .sdlc/plans, research and acceptance for the goal's own files. See Cost and time.

Can two people run it on one repository?

Yes. Turn on the ledger so each loop sees what the others hold, and each person's loop works the issues assigned to them. See As a team.

My tests need installed dependencies. Will they run?

A goal's fresh worktree has no node_modules or virtual environment, so a heavy verify command pays that cost per goal and a relative interpreter path fails. Use an absolute path or a wrapper script.

Why did it not pick my issue?

See the checklist above. The usual causes are no sdlc:goal label, an issue not assigned to you, and an open prerequisite.

Where do I ask for help?

Run /sigma-doctor and keep its output, then open an issue in the repository. Leave out anything private.

Technical detail

The doctor's rows and fixes were read from its code and skill text; the symptoms above were read from the documentation, not reproduced one by one in a fresh run. Measured by a manual read: the 403 on the protection read of a free-plan private repository. Not measured: a run with no network, and the uninstall and update paths on Codex, Cursor and Antigravity. Sources: cloud sessions, enforcement, platform support, label model.
